experiment: Replace all Cranelift-generated fused loops, cached scalar kernels and specialized SIMD reductions with Inkwell/LLVM.
llvm_source: Dirty source captured in llvm-source.tar.gz; llvm.patch excludes the new llvm.rs, which is present in the archive and metadata hashes.

toolchain.optimization: default<O3> and MCJIT Aggressive; host CPU/features; no fast math; constrained floating arithmetic to preserve tested NaN behavior

measurement.summary: Median of replica medians; ranges are observed replica minima/maxima, not confidence intervals. Total uses median of paired preparation+execution samples.

scope: Resident-input whole-engine benchmark; input generation, full correctness checking and output destruction outside timed regions. Each process validates all output rows before timed samples; timed samples check output count. Generated-library prewarm is measured separately once per process.
limitations: First LLVM port preserving graph lowering and runtime structure, not a separately tuned LLVM execution engine.
Single-thread results generally stable; some four-worker cases retain large run-to-run variation on this desktop host.
No disk IO, cold data, or varied row counts tested.
LLVM full compile includes compiling both the general loop and specialized reduction when eligible, as did the Cranelift baseline.
Only Linux x86_64 was built and tested; LLVM 19 development tools are now a build dependency.
